summary: The High Court allowed a writ of quo warranto, holding that the State government lacked authority to re-appoint the Vice-Chancellor of Calcutta University under Section 8 or Section 60 of the Calcutta University Act, 1979. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's analysis that only the Chancellor has the power to appoint or re-appoint the VC, and the State's invocation of Section 60 was impermissible. The re-appointment made on 27 August 2021 was declared illegal.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 8 of the Calcutta University Act, 1979
Section 60 of the Calcutta University Act, 1979
Rule 9 of the West Bengal State Universities (Terms and Conditions of Service of the Vice Chancellors and the Manner and Procedure of Official Communication) Rules 2019
UGC (Minimum qualifications for appointment of teachers and other academic staff in University and Colleges and measures for the maintenance of standards in Higher Education) Regulations 2018
Article 14 of the Constitution of India
Article 226 of the Constitution of India
Central Electricity Supply Utility of Odisha v. Dhobei Sahoo (2014) 1 SCC 161
Bharati Reddy v. State of Karnataka (2018) 6 SCC 162
Ghambirdan K Gadhvi v. State of Gujarat (2022) 5 SCC 179
final_judgment: The appeal was dismissed, and the High Court's judgment setting aside the re-appointment of the Vice-Chancellor was upheld.
